chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the son of Adam as hollow.

key_terms.أَجْوَفَ: Hollow, empty, or having a cavity; describing the nature of human creation as a vessel.
key_terms.ابْنَ آدَمَ: Son of Adam; a common term for humanity in Islamic texts.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; honorific titles for Allah.

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the son of Adam is created hollow?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) uses the term 'ajwaf' to describe the inherent physical and spiritual emptiness of humanity, emphasizing the necessity of divine sustenance. Shia scholars interpret this not merely as a biological fact but as a theological reminder that humans are vessels requiring the filling of faith (iman) and knowledge (ilm) to achieve perfection. This concept underscores the dependency of the created being on the Creator for both physical survival and spiritual fulfillment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created the son of Adam<sup>as</sup> as hollow’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has created the child of Adam hollow.’”
